ids: test/control_plane/watcher.test.ts::seam liveness (target-only) > watcher uuid4Hex names the refused heartbeats action row
target_only_tests.note: Target-only. watcher.ts routes its one nondeterministic call -- the generated action_id on the refusal path -- through watcherSeams.uuid4Hex (D-0014). interlock's suite never patches uuid (every refusal case compares the recorded action_id against the one the refusal carries, so it pins the id's consistency and never its value), so this liveness test has no source counterpart and is not counted as ported coverage. It exists because a seam nothing routes through is worse than no seam: it looks like a control point while production goes around it.

entries.reason: `inspect.signature(heartbeat).parameters` has no runtime analogue: an options object's keys exist only in the type. Translated the way migrator.test.ts translates `dir(m)` -- two halves: the runtime arity (`heartbeat.length === 2`, which a positional `resource` argument would change) and a scan of the declaration's own source text in src/control_plane/watcher.ts, asserting no `readonly <name>:` option is `resource` and that the whole signature text does not match /resource/i. Anti-vacuity: the declaration regex must match (expect(declaration).not.toBeNull()) and the scanned parameter list must contain `scopeId`, so a scan that matched nothing fails instead of passing. Strictly stronger than the source's key-membership check (it also excludes a resource-typed or resource-named positional).

entries.reason: `Path(watcher.__file__).read_text()` with `"time.time" not in source` / `"import time" not in source` names Python clock readers that do not exist in TypeScript. Same scan, over src/control_plane/watcher.ts's own text, against the names a TypeScript clock read would have to use: `Date.now`, `new Date`, `performance.now`, `hrtime`, `node:timers`. Anti-vacuity: `source.length > 0` and `source` must contain `export function heartbeat`, so an unreadable/empty/wrong file fails instead of passing every `not.toContain`. Deliberately NOT extended to SQL clock functions (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP/unixepoch/...): the source's scan covers language-level clock reads only, and adding them would make the case stricter than its source.

inherited_limitations.topic: The incident-query projections return camelCase objects where the source returns mappings keyed by the database's own column names.
inherited_limitations.detail: silentScopes / uncoveredScopes / errorStreakScopes return frozen camelCase records; interlock returns MappingProxyType rows keyed by scope_id, silent_for_ms and so on. Same position already recorded for ci_ingest.ts's scopeVerdicts -- faithful in VALUE, differing only in the shape a TypeScript caller sees. Settling it one way belongs in a convention change applied everywhere at once, not inside a translation.

inherited_limitations.topic: Numeric columns are read with Number() rather than re-narrowed to Python's int().
inherited_limitations.detail: The source applies int() at these reads and the port does not; for a well-formed INTEGER column the two agree, and they differ only for a row whose stored value violates the column's declared type, which no supported code path can write. Stated this way deliberately: an earlier draft of this entry described the source as applying no coercion, which would have made the disclosure unverifiable against the Python.

inherited_limitations.topic: requireIdentifier rejects on value.trim() where the source uses str.strip().
inherited_limitations.detail: Python's str.strip() also removes U+001C-U+001F and U+0085, which JavaScript's trim() does not, so a string consisting only of those characters is refused by the source and accepted here. Unreachable from any ported case; recorded rather than left as an undisclosed asymmetry.

inherited_limitations.topic: A held-epoch tuple is read without the source's absent-value hazard.
inherited_limitations.detail: interlock indexes held_epoch[0] / held_epoch[1] with no None guard, so a None there raises a TypeError rather than a typed refusal. The port's types make the absent case explicit. This is the port being stricter than its source (criterion 5), recorded rather than silently kept.
